scenes.heading: What a creator manager actually does

sents.d: What a creator manager actually does
The role is closer to a talent manager or social media manager than most newcomers expect.

scenes.heading: The business side of an account

sents.d: A creator manager typically handles the business operations side of a subscription-platform account: scheduling and posting content, responding to subscriber messages, running promotions, and tracking performance — so the creator can focus on producing content.
The specific split of responsibilities varies a lot by agreement.
Some managers only handle messaging and scheduling; others also run marketing, negotiate collaborations, or manage a small team supporting one creator.

This is fundamentally a client-services business built on trust and access to sensitive accounts, closer in structure to being a talent manager or a specialized social media manager than to typical content creation work.

take: Creator management is a client-services business built on trust.
